description:
FLAMENCE | Flame in Freefall

FLAMENCE is a two-person team participating in the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge. Our mission is to explore microgravity combustion and space fire safety using AI-assisted analysis, scientific data visualization, and interactive web technologies. We aim to transform NASA's combustion research into clear, engaging insights that support a better understanding of fire behavior in space and safer human space exploration.

FLAMENCE — Understanding Fire Beyond Earth.
summary:
FLAMENCE — Fire in Microgravity is an interactive, evidence-led research platform developed for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 under the Flame in Freefall challenge.

The platform transforms complex NASA microgravity combustion research into accessible scientific insights through 22 interconnected research sections, Earth-versus-ISS flame visualizations, independent Fuel Lab environments, source-linked evidence retrieval, and an AI-assisted research interface.

FLAMENCE integrates NASA PSI-69 FLEX experimental records, including 274 combustion tests and 237 selected droplet measurements. Its burning-rate research model was evaluated using 204 eligible tests across 89 condition groups and achieved a median mean absolute error of 0.0486 mm²/s, compared with 0.1006 mm²/s for a fuel-median baseline.

Three saved-source SHA-256 checks matched their recorded reference hashes. The platform distinguishes experimental evidence from conceptual simulations and clearly states the limits of its predictive capabilities.

FLAMENCE aims to make combustion research more transparent, reproducible, and useful for understanding spacecraft fire-safety challenges.
details:
The Problem

Fire behaves differently in microgravity because buoyancy-driven convection is greatly reduced. NASA has investigated droplet combustion, flame spread, extinction, ventilation, and smoke behavior through experiments such as FLEX, BASS-II, ACME, SoFIE, and Saffire.

These findings are spread across experimental datasets, technical publications, and research archives. FLAMENCE addresses the challenge of making this evidence easier to find, compare, understand, and evaluate.

Our Solution

FLAMENCE — Fire in Microgravity is a publicly accessible scientific research platform combining 22 interactive sections with experimental-data analysis, AI-assisted research, evidence retrieval, and educational combustion visualizations.

Core features:

  • Flame Lab: Illustrates the differences between buoyancy-driven and microgravity combustion across five conceptual environments.
  • Fuel Lab: Provides independent Earth and ISS combustion chambers, fuel selections, and adjustable oxygen and airflow controls.
  • NASA Data Lab: Explores 274 NASA PSI-69 FLEX experimental records, including 157 methanol and 117 heptane tests.
  • Droplet Analysis: Examines 237 selected measurements from FLEX-001 (127) and FLEX-007 (110), with source reconciliation.
  • Predictive Research: Uses a ridge regression burning-rate model evaluated on 204 usable FLEX records across 89 condition groups.
  • Evidence Intelligence: Organizes and retrieves scientific findings through source-linked research records.
  • Mission Intelligence: Supports educational investigations across different hypothetical mission environments.
  • AI Research Assistant: Helps users navigate the platform and interpret research while distinguishing documented evidence from general AI explanations.

Scientific Evaluation

The FLEX burning-rate model was evaluated using 12 overlapping grouped-holdout folds. Its median mean absolute error was 0.0486 mm²/s compared with 0.1006 mm²/s for a fuel-median baseline, approximately a 52% reduction.

All three saved-source SHA-256 checks matched their recorded reference hashes. The 237 selected FLEX-001/FLEX-007 measurements were reconciled to the team's saved source files. The original independently reviewable NASA-to-S3 download-network trace is not bundled.

These results support reproducibility and within-dataset evaluation. They do not establish flight qualification, NASA endorsement, or reliable prediction across all spacecraft environments.

Technology and Innovation

FLAMENCE was developed using HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Python-based analysis, Node.js testing, Cloudflare Workers, and Cloudflare Workers AI.

Its innovation lies in bringing scientific evidence retrieval, interactive combustion exploration, dataset auditing, predictive-model evaluation, and AI-assisted interpretation together in one accessible interface.

Unlike a static research catalogue, FLAMENCE enables users to explore different aspects of combustion research and examine the evidence and limitations behind numerical results.

Intended Impact

FLAMENCE aims to improve access to microgravity combustion research for students, researchers, educators, and space-technology enthusiasts. It offers a foundation for future work incorporating additional independently verified NASA datasets, partial-gravity studies, and stronger model validation.

Live application: https://flamence.flamence-labs.workers.dev/

Source code: https://github.com/jamalmohamedmr/FLAMENCE

Created by M Mohamed Afris & MR Jamal Mohamed.
